packet.headline_seed: 'Anti-ICE' Army veteran set fire outside Manhattan federal building, say officials
packet.description_seed: Andrew Arrabaca, 43, was armed with two axes, a machete, three knives and fireworks, says the FBI.

what: 'Anti-ICE' Army veteran set fire outside Manhattan federal building, say officials

clean_source_blocks.text: A former US Army soldier toting an anti-ICE sign set off fireworks, lit a fire and shot a pellet gun outside a Manhattan federal office building, injuring three people before security officers subdued him, authorities say. Officials identified the suspect ‌as Andrew Arrabaca, a 43-year-old US Army veteran living in Harlem. On Monday morning, a man appeared to pour petrol from a bucket onto the stairs of 26 Federal Plaza, an office tower that also houses the FBI's New York field office, then set it ‌on fire, according ‌to authorities ⁠and local news videos. The suspect, who brought anti-Immigration and Customs Enforcement literature, also ​ignited fireworks, authorities said. The Department of Homeland Security said on X that a Federal Protective Service officer who detained the man, described by DHS as "an anti-ICE rioter," sustained minor injuries.

Fox News correspondent Nate Foy details an anti-ICE attack, where the suspect allegedly used fireworks, a pellet gun, and gasoline, to light a fire outside a Manhattan federal building on 'Special Report.' Former U.S. Army soldier Andrew Arrabaca is in custody for an anti-ICE, anti-government attack at a federal building in downtown Manhattan. Nate Foy reports the suspect used fireworks, a pellet gun, and gasoline, injuring three, including an immigrant. FBI officials describe Arabac as an anti-American extremist. Attacks on ICE officers are up 1,300%, raising concerns about anti-government sentiment.

A former US Army soldier has been arrested after igniting a fire in front of a federal building in New York City, says the FBI. Andrew Arrabaca, 43, allegedly shot a pellet gun and set off fireworks on Monday morning at 26 Federal Plaza, where the FBI, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and US Citizenship and Immigration Services have offices. Federal agents tackled the suspect, who they say was armed with a machete and other weapons. Three people sustained minor injuries in the incident, including an immigrant who was attending a status hearing, said the FBI. The lower Manhattan site has become a flashpoint for protests against President Donald Trump's immigration policies.

The suspect, whom the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) called an "anti-ICE rioter", launched fireworks before pouring an accelerant on the stairs of an entrance to the building, causing a fire. The BBC has contacted DHS for comment. Arrabaca "made several anti-government and anti-ICE statements during the incident", the FBI said. FBI New York Assistant Director James Barnacle said during a news conference that Arrabaca was armed with two axes, a machete, three knives and fireworks. He fired about five to seven pellets from an airsoft gun in the direction of the building, Barnacle said. Of those injured, two were government employees, Barnacle said. DHS said a bystander was grazed, and a security officer who tackled and detained Arrabaca sustained minor injuries. "He is an anti-American, anti-government extremist," Barnacle added.

[Lähde: BBC World | URL: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c1m1rr90dzxo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss]
A former US Army soldier has been arrested after igniting a fire in front of a federal building in New York City, says the FBI.

Andrew Arrabaca, 43, allegedly shot a pellet gun and set off fireworks on Monday morning at 26 Federal Plaza, where the FBI, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and US Citizenship and Immigration Services have offices.

Federal agents tackled the suspect, who they say was armed with a machete and other weapons.

Three people sustained minor injuries in the incident, including an immigrant who was attending a status hearing, said the FBI. The lower Manhattan site has become a flashpoint for protests against President Donald Trump's immigration policies.

The suspect, whom the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) called an "anti-ICE rioter", launched fireworks before pouring an accelerant on the stairs of an entrance to the building, causing a fire. The BBC has contacted DHS for comment.

Arrabaca "made several anti-government and anti-ICE statements during the incident", the FBI said.

FBI New York Assistant Director James Barnacle said during a news conference that Arrabaca was armed with two axes, a machete, three knives and fireworks.

He fired about five to seven pellets from an airsoft gun in the direction of the building, Barnacle said.

Of those injured, two were government employees, Barnacle said.

DHS said a bystander was grazed, and a security officer who tackled and detained Arrabaca sustained minor injuries.

"He is an anti-American, anti-government extremist," Barnacle added.

Arrabaca, of Poughkeepsie, New York state, served in the regular Army from 2001-04 and in the Army National Guard-New York from 2004-05, according to the BBC's US partner CBS.

He did not have any deployments and left the Army with the rank of specialist.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani called the incident "deeply disturbing" in a post on X.

"Our administration will continue to ensure that every New Yorker is safe in their city - and hold accountable any who threaten that," he said.

A former US Army soldier toting an anti-ICE sign set off fireworks, lit a fire and shot a pellet gun outside a Manhattan federal office building, injuring three people before security officers subdued him, authorities say.

Officials identified the suspect ‌as Andrew Arrabaca, a 43-year-old US Army veteran living in Harlem.

On Monday morning, a man appeared to pour petrol from a bucket onto the stairs of 26 Federal Plaza, an office tower that also houses the FBI's New York field office, then set it ‌on fire, according ‌to authorities ⁠and local news videos.

The suspect, who brought anti-Immigration and Customs Enforcement literature, also ​ignited fireworks, authorities said.

The Department of Homeland Security said on X that a Federal Protective Service officer who detained the man, described by DHS as "an anti-ICE rioter," sustained minor injuries.

Two other people were also lightly injured, James Barnacle, FBI assistant director in charge of the ⁠New York office, told a news conference.

Barnacle ‌said ​the suspect was "an anti-American, anti-government extremist."

James McDonald, deputy US Attorney for the Southern District of ​New York, said ‌an investigation was continuing and no decision has yet been made on charges.

​Arrabaca could not be reached for comment, and it was unclear if he had a lawyer.

Arrabaca served in the Army from 2001 to 2005 and ​serviced Patriot ​missile systems, officials said.

Investigators traced the suspect to his home ‌in Harlem, authorities said. Officials said he arrived in New York by subway on Sunday and spent the night on the street in Lower Manhattan.

"What occurred outside 26 Federal Plaza this morning was deeply disturbing. I'm relieved no one was seriously injured and that a suspect ​is in custody," New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani told reporters.

payload.title: Entinen sotilas pidätettiin liittovaltion virastotalon palosta Manhattanilla
payload.summary: Andrew Arrabacan epäillään sytyttäneen tulipalon ja ampuneen airsoft-aseella liittovaltion virastotalon edustalla New Yorkissa. Kolme ihmistä loukkaantui lievästi.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain armeijan entinen sotilas Andrew Arrabaca, 43, on pidätetty New Yorkissa sen jälkeen, kun hänen epäillään sytyttäneen tulipalon liittovaltion virastotalon portailla Ala-Manhattanilla maanantaiaamuna. FBI:n mukaan hän laukaisi myös ilotulitteita ja ampui airsoft-aseella rakennusta kohti. Kolme ihmistä sai välikohtauksessa lieviä vammoja. Viranomaisten mukaan Arrabaca asuu Harlemissa.

## Palava neste sytytettiin portailla

Viranomaisten mukaan Arrabaca kaatoi ämpäristä palavaa nestettä 26 Federal Plaza -toimistotornin sisäänkäynnin portaille ja sytytti sen. Ennen palon syttymistä hän laukaisi ilotulitteita. Tapahtumat näkyivät myös paikallisten uutismedioiden julkaisemilla videoilla. FBI:n New Yorkin kenttätoimiston apulaisjohtaja James Barnacle kertoi epäillyn ampuneen noin viidestä seitsemään kuulaa airsoft-aseella rakennuksen suuntaan.

Turvallisuusvirkailija taltutti Arrabacan, minkä jälkeen tämä otettiin kiinni tapahtumapaikalla. Sisäisen turvallisuuden ministeriön mukaan hänet pysäyttänyt henkilö oli liittovaltion suojelupalvelun virkailija, joka loukkaantui kiinnioton yhteydessä lievästi. Barnaclen mukaan Arrabacalla oli mukanaan kaksi kirvestä, viidakkoveitsi, kolme muuta veistä ja ilotulitteita. Hänen kerrottiin myös kantaneen ICE:n vastaista kylttiä ja muuta aineistoa.

FBI avasi tapahtumien kulkua New Yorkissa järjestetyssä tiedotustilaisuudessa. Sisäisen turvallisuuden ministeriö puolestaan kertoi turvallisuusvirkailijan vammoista viestipalvelu X:ssä. FBI:n mukaan Arrabaca esitti tapahtuman aikana useita hallinnon ja ICE:n vastaisia lausumia. Ministeriö kuvaili häntä ICE:n vastaiseksi mellakoitsijaksi. Barnacle puolestaan kutsui Arrabacaa Yhdysvaltain ja hallinnon vastaiseksi ääriajattelijaksi. Molemmat ilmaukset olivat viranomaisten omia luonnehdintoja epäillystä.

## Kolme ihmistä loukkaantui lievästi

FBI:n mukaan loukkaantuneista kaksi oli valtion työntekijöitä. Joukossa oli myös maahanmuuttaja, joka oli saapunut rakennukseen maahanmuuttostatustaan koskevaan käsittelyyn. Sisäisen turvallisuuden ministeriö kertoi lisäksi sivullisen saaneen hipaisuosuman. Viranomaisten tiedoissa kaikki kolme vammaa kuvattiin lieviksi.

26 Federal Plaza -rakennuksessa toimivat FBI:n New Yorkin kenttätoimisto, Yhdysvaltain maahanmuutto- ja tullivalvontavirasto ICE sekä kansalaisuus- ja maahanmuuttovirasto USCIS. Ala-Manhattanilla sijaitsevasta rakennuksesta on tullut presidentti Donald Trumpin maahanmuuttopolitiikkaa vastustavien mielenosoitusten keskeinen paikka. Rakennuksen edusta oli protestien näyttämönä jo ennen maanantaista välikohtausta.

article.source_text:
A former US Army soldier toting an anti-ICE sign set off fireworks, lit a fire and shot a pellet gun outside a Manhattan federal office building, injuring three people before security officers subdued him, authorities say. Officials identified the suspect ‌as Andrew Arrabaca, a 43-year-old US Army veteran living in Harlem. On Monday morning, a man appeared to pour petrol from a bucket onto the stairs of 26 Federal Plaza, an office tower that also houses the FBI's New York field office, then set it ‌on fire, according ‌to authorities ⁠and local news videos. The suspect, who brought anti-Immigration and Customs Enforcement literature, also ​ignited fireworks, authorities said. The Department of Homeland Security said on X that a Federal Protective Service officer who detained the man, described by DHS as "an anti-ICE rioter," sustained minor injuries.

Fox News correspondent Nate Foy details an anti-ICE attack, where the suspect allegedly used fireworks, a pellet gun, and gasoline, to light a fire outside a Manhattan federal building on 'Special Report.' Former U.S. Army soldier Andrew Arrabaca is in custody for an anti-ICE, anti-government attack at a federal building in downtown Manhattan. Nate Foy reports the suspect used fireworks, a pellet gun, and gasoline, injuring three, including an immigrant. FBI officials describe Arabac as an anti-American extremist. Attacks on ICE officers are up 1,300%, raising concerns about anti-government sentiment.

A former US Army soldier has been arrested after igniting a fire in front of a federal building in New York City, says the FBI. Andrew Arrabaca, 43, allegedly shot a pellet gun and set off fireworks on Monday morning at 26 Federal Plaza, where the FBI, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and US Citizenship and Immigration Services have offices. Federal agents tackled the suspect, who they say was armed with a machete and other weapons. Three people sustained minor injuries in the incident, including an immigrant who was attending a status hearing, said the FBI. The lower Manhattan site has become a flashpoint for protests against President Donald Trump's immigration policies.

The suspect, whom the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) called an "anti-ICE rioter", launched fireworks before pouring an accelerant on the stairs of an entrance to the building, causing a fire. The BBC has contacted DHS for comment. Arrabaca "made several anti-government and anti-ICE statements during the incident", the FBI said. FBI New York Assistant Director James Barnacle said during a news conference that Arrabaca was armed with two axes, a machete, three knives and fireworks. He fired about five to seven pellets from an airsoft gun in the direction of the building, Barnacle said. Of those injured, two were government employees, Barnacle said. DHS said a bystander was grazed, and a security officer who tackled and detained Arrabaca sustained minor injuries. "He is an anti-American, anti-government extremist," Barnacle added.
